item.family_title: Bloch's law, its lattice correction, and the spherical magnetization law
item.manuscript: Spontaneous magnetization in the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet (24 Sep 2026)
item.name: Spliced stable permutation symbol F_pi(x,y) = prod_i (x_i + y_{pi(i)})
item.trace_grade: N3 candidate (borderline N2), F1/F5; pivot PV3, eureka candidate E1
item.paper_location: build/source/sections/02-pin-test.tex: Lemma lem:pin-stability-closure, Lemma lem:pin-partial-symmetrization, Lemma lem:pin-exchange-symbol, eq. pin-layered-symbol, Lemma lem:pin-splicing, Lemma lem:pin-presence, Proposition prop:pin-test

definition.symbol: For a permutation pi of a finite set V, F_pi(x,y) := prod_{i in V} (x_i + y_{pi(i)}), a multiaffine polynomial in 2|V| variables (one input variable x_i and one output variable y_j per point). For a random pi, the law symbol is E F_pi.
definition.stability_lemma: If pi is a finite product of independent Bernoulli(u) transpositions and deterministic permutations (or a limit of such laws: finite-time Poisson exchange processes, uniform permutations on subsets, and independent products of these), then E F_pi is stable, i.e. it has no zero when every variable lies in the open upper half-plane. Proof: the identity symbol is a product of nonvanishing factors; composing with a Bernoulli transposition is the partial symmetrization (1-u)F + u tauF in two output variables, which preserves stability (BBL Thm 4.20; the paper gives an elementary two-variable section proof); limits by Hurwitz.
definition.layering: Cut the periodic time circle of Toth's exchange picture at every pin time; V = disjoint union of slot layers at the cuts; the layer-to-layer maps are independent, so the layered symbol F_V = E prod_{i in V}(x_i + y_{pi(i)}) is a product of stable interval symbols, hence stable.
definition.splicing: Eliminate an unpinned vertex q by setting x_q = y_q = t and extracting the coefficient of t. On a path i -> q -> j the factors (x_i + t)(t + y_j) give x_i + y_j (the path is spliced); on a fixed point the factor x_q + y_q = 2t gives the factor 2. Removing all non-pins gives F_P(x,y) = E_b[ 2^{n_P(pi)} prod_{i in P}(x_i + y_{sigma(i)}) ], where sigma is the next-pin permutation and n_P is the number of cycles missing P. Each closed cycle that avoids the pins contributes exactly the Heisenberg (Toth) cycle weight 2 = dim C^2, so the spliced symbol encodes the PINNED, CYCLE-WEIGHTED law P_P, with no stability lost (identification and differentiation are closure operations).
definition.output_extraction: G_T(y) = E_P prod_{i in T} y_{sigma(i)} = Z_P^{-1} (prod_{i in P\T} d/dx_i) F_P |_{x=0} is the stable subset generating polynomial of sigma(T); stability gives P_P(J subset sigma(T)) <= prod_j P_P(j in sigma(T)) (BBL Thm 4.9 consequence).
definition.decisive_use: Proposition prop:pin-test: P_E(T subset B_E) <= (2r)^{|T|}, where B_E is the union of cycles avoiding the pin set E and r is the mean return fraction. The factor 2^{|T|} comes from comparing pin laws P_E and P_{E u T}.
definition.companion_variant: The spherical-law companion (Oct 5) uses the disk form E prod_i (1 + x_i y_{pi(i)}), zero-free on |x_i|,|y_i| < 1 (Cayley transform of the half-plane symbol), and contracts output with next-layer input via A + Bx + Cy + Dxy -> A + D (Asano-Ruelle contraction) to prove zero-free layered traces (Lemma trace-zero-free).

obstruction_dissolved: The cycle-weighted interchange measure (weight theta^{#cycles}, theta = 2 for Toth's Heisenberg representation) has no known negative-dependence / strongly Rayleigh structure: BBL-type stability is known for unweighted symmetric exclusion and interchange (theta = 1), and the weight 2^{#cycles} is a global, non-local reweighting that partial symmetrization does not see. The model's preceding route (holes + exterior powers, determinants/signed minors) computes first moments but cannot bound the POSITIVE event that many test points simultaneously lie on cycles avoiding the pins (trace conflict C9). Without a positivity-preserving encoding, one cannot get a product bound (2r)^m for the simultaneous event, and density/scalar bootstrap arguments are defeated by trapping walls and arbitrary phase fractions (C7, C8). The spliced symbol solves both: it carries a positivity-preserving (stable) encoding through the unweighted exchange layers where BBL applies, and the splicing contraction itself manufactures the factor 2 per closed cycle, so the weighted pinned law inherits stability.
abstract_mechanism: Encode a random bijection by its 'two-sided symbol' prod_i (in_i + out_{pi(i)}), which is a stability-preserving (real-stable) object under independent local mixing moves. Compose independent layers by multiplying symbols in disjoint variables, then take a trace by contracting each output variable with the matching input variable (identify and extract the linear coefficient). The contraction is a stability-preserving closure operation that splices paths and assigns every closed loop a fixed weight equal to the trace of the identity on a 2-dimensional space (here 2). The result is a stable generating polynomial for a GLOBALLY loop-weighted measure, from which negative dependence (product bounds on simultaneous positive events) follows. Field-independently: 'a loop-weighted measure whose loop weight equals tr(I) on a two-state space is a contraction (partial trace) of a product of stable local transfer symbols, so it inherits negative dependence from the local moves.' Equivalently (precedent view): the law symbol is the Borcea-Branden symbol T[prod(z_i + w_i)] of the permutation-averaging operator, and splicing is the half-plane form of an Asano contraction, i.e. a stable-polynomial transfer-matrix trace.

candidates.problem: Long-range order / long loops for Ueltschi's random loop model with theta = 2 and u in (1/2, 1), i.e. the spin-1/2 XXZ-type ferromagnets -sum (S1S1 + S3S3 + Delta S2S2) with Delta = 2u-1 in (0,1) (easy-plane anisotropic ferromagnet) on Z^d, d >= 3, at low temperature.
candidates.reference: D. Ueltschi, Random loop representations for quantum spin systems, J. Math. Phys. 54 (2013), arXiv:1301.0811; Betz-Klippel-Nauth, Improved bounds for connection probabilities in random loop models, arXiv:2503.17857 (Thm 2.1 restricted to u in [0,1/2]).
candidates.status: open for u in (1/2,1) (reflection-positivity methods cover u in [0,1/2]; u = 1 is the OAI family-271 result).
candidates.obstruction_match: Exactly the same: no reflection positivity, theta = 2 loop weight, and need for negative dependence of loop-hitting events. Loops now carry crosses (prob u) and double bars (prob 1-u); double bars make loops non-orientable, so the next-pin map is a Brauer pairing, not a permutation.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: Replace F_pi by the Brauer symbol prod_{pairs {a,b}} (z_a + z_b) over the pairing of the 2n endpoints of a layer. A double bar on strands i,j acts on the output variables by Q: A + B y_i + C y_j + D y_i y_j -> (B + C)(y_i + y_j). I checked (this analysis) that the two-strand mixture symbol (1-u-v)(y1+w1)(y2+w2) + u(y2+w1)(y1+w2) + v(w1+w2)(y1+y2) is a homogeneous quadratic with Gram eigenvalues {2, -2u, -2v, -2(1-u-v)} (times 1/2), hence Lorentzian, hence real stable for ALL u,v >= 0, u+v <= 1; by the Borcea-Branden symbol theorem the step preserves stability, and random 3-strand Brauer laws tested numerically are stable. Splicing still gives factor 2 per closed loop. So the stability half of the device transfers to the whole XXZ family. Missing piece: output extraction. For pairings, the event 'T-endpoints are matched among themselves' is not a subset-presence event; one needs a new extraction (e.g. lowest-degree homogeneous part in T variables, which is stable and isolates exactly the configurations with no E-T pairs) and a pairing analogue of the presence inequality. The rest of the OAI proof (hole walks, return energy, Nash/flows) would also need an easy-plane version.
candidates.expected_payoff: resolves an open regime (new theorem) if the extraction and the geometric part go through; at minimum a negative-dependence lemma for the theta=2 Brauer loop measure (new).

candidates.problem: Spontaneous magnetization (macroscopic theta=2 cycles) of the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet on other transient geometries: regular trees of every degree >= 3, nonamenable transitive graphs, Cayley graphs of polynomial growth of degree >= 3, and long-range couplings J(x) ~ |x|^{-alpha} in d = 1, 2.
candidates.reference: Bjornberg-Ueltschi, Critical temperature of Heisenberg models on regular trees, via random loops, arXiv:1803.11430 (large degree only); Hammond & Hegde, interchange on trees (theta=1); Adamczak-Kotowski-Milos, Hamming graph H(2,n) (AIHP 57, 2021); Bjornberg, Large cycles in random permutations related to the Heisenberg model, arXiv:1505.06716 (complete graph).
candidates.status: open for general transient graphs and small-degree trees (ferromagnet lacks reflection positivity; only mean-field-type graphs are solved).
candidates.obstruction_match: Identical; the device is purely combinatorial and graph-independent (Lemma pin-exchange-symbol makes no spatial assumption; the spherical companion stresses this).
candidates.adaptation_sketch: Use the pin test verbatim. Replace the d >= 3 lattice geometry (Nash inequality, flows around hulls, two-end leakage) by the corresponding transience/isoperimetric input of the target graph; on trees and nonamenable graphs the return-probability input is far easier (exponential decay of the return fraction r).
candidates.expected_payoff: new theorems (spontaneous magnetization on new graph classes); simplifies Bjornberg-Ueltschi-type large-degree arguments.
candidates.difficulty: medium-high (device transfers trivially; the leakage/escape part is graph-specific)

candidates.problem: Lee-Yang / zero-free regions for quantum Heisenberg partition functions, and Barvinok-type approximation algorithms that need them (complex field, complex time strips).
candidates.reference: Suzuki & Fisher, J. Math. Phys. 12 (1971) 235; Asano 1970; Harrow-Mehraban-Soleimanifar, Classical algorithms, correlation decay, and complex zeros of partition functions of quantum many-body systems, arXiv:1910.09071 (Thm 45-47 rely on SF71 via a classical mapping); spherical-law companion, Lemma trace-zero-free.
candidates.status: Lee-Yang circle theorem known (SF71); zero-free strips relevant for low-temperature pressure tangents are partly new (spherical companion).
candidates.obstruction_match: Need zero-freeness of a quantum trace; the disk form E prod(1 + x_i y_{pi(i)}) plus Asano contraction A + D gives exactly that, directly in the loop representation without a Trotter classical mapping.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: Insert single-slot matrices mapping the closed disk into the open disk between permutation layers and contract (as in the spherical companion). Target: a one-page proof of the SF71 Lee-Yang theorem for the isotropic spin-S ferromagnet, and zero-free strips for anisotropic/inhomogeneous couplings that HMS's algorithm needs.
candidates.expected_payoff: simplifies a known proof (SF71); possibly new zero-free regions (complex anisotropy or complex time) with algorithmic consequences.
candidates.confidence: medium-high for the re-proof, low for new regions

candidates.problem: Poisson-Dirichlet PD(2) law of macroscopic cycle lengths in Toth's theta=2 model on Z^d, d >= 3 (Goldschmidt-Ueltschi-Windridge conjecture); also existence of macroscopic cycles at all large beta on the torus.
candidates.reference: Goldschmidt, Ueltschi, Windridge, Quantum Heisenberg models and their probabilistic representations, arXiv:1104.0983; Elboim-Sly, arXiv:2211.17023 (theta=1, d>=5, PD(1) on tori).
candidates.status: open for theta=2 on Z^d (OAI family 271 gives magnetization >= S/4 hence some macroscopic loops, not their law).
candidates.obstruction_match: Partial: the pin test bounds simultaneous avoidance events and gives negative dependence of next-pin outputs under the weighted law, a needed ingredient for split-merge / 'loops hit many test points' arguments.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: Use stable spliced symbols with pins on a sparse grid to control joint loop-hitting of many test points, then feed into a split-merge comparison (Schramm's method) for cycle lengths. Weight-2 negative dependence would replace Elboim-Sly's cyclic-time random-walk coupling for the clustering step.
candidates.expected_payoff: possible new bound or route toward PD(2); full resolution unlikely from the device alone.

candidates.problem: Negative dependence for card-shuffle projections and symmetric exclusion: S_k block shuffles (projection onto first K cards is strongly Rayleigh), Thorp shuffle occupancy (release family 238), SEP with open boundaries/reservoirs.
candidates.reference: Nestoridi-Priestley-Schmid, The S_k shuffle block dynamics, arXiv:2304.02588 (Cor. 3.6 via Borcea-Branden 2009 Thm 1.2 + Trotter); Salez and Tran on SEP with open boundaries; release family 238 (Routing densities ... Thorp sweeps, sec 04-certificate).
candidates.obstruction_match: Unspliced half of the device only: stable law symbols of Bernoulli/uniform block permutations and output extraction give SR of pi(A) for deterministic A directly.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: lawSymbol + stable_lawSymbol_bernoulli + stable_lawSymbol_limit (uniform block = limit) + stable_outputSymbol. For reservoirs: model each boundary reservoir as pinned vertices and splice; the pin weight changes, so this needs checking.
candidates.expected_payoff: simplifies known proofs (removes the BB symbol theorem / Obreschkoff machinery for deterministic starts).
candidates.confidence: high (for SR of images from deterministic starts)

candidates.problem: Classical efficient approximation (FPRAS) of the partition function / Gibbs sampling of the ferromagnetic quantum Heisenberg model (isotropic, ZZ terms included).
candidates.reference: Bravyi & Gosset, Polynomial-time classical simulation of quantum ferromagnets, PRL 119 (2017), arXiv:1612.05602 (covers XY/transverse Ising, not ZZ); HMS arXiv:1910.09071; Bravyi-Gosset-Liu-Wong, arXiv:2607.14401 (quantum algorithm for Suzuki-Fisher family).
candidates.status: open (no classical FPRAS known for the isotropic Heisenberg ferromagnet at all temperatures).
candidates.obstruction_match: Weak: stability/negative dependence is the engine of spectral-independence rapid-mixing proofs, but the device gives stability of pinned output polynomials, not of the full loop configuration measure.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: Self-reduce Z_E/Z_{E u T} via pin laws; try to prove spectral independence for a pin-resampling chain using stability of F_P. Unclear.

candidates.problem: Antiferromagnet / Aizenman-Nachtergaele loops (u = 0) beyond reflection positivity: Neel order for bipartite finite-range or non-reflection-symmetric couplings.
candidates.reference: Aizenman & Nachtergaele, CMP 164 (1994); Ueltschi 2013; Dyson-Lieb-Simon 1978; Kennedy-Lieb-Shastry 1988.
candidates.status: nearest-neighbour Z^d, d >= 3 is covered by RP (gamma = 2 < 2.22 in Betz-Klippel-Nauth's d=3 table); non-RP couplings open.
candidates.obstruction_match: On bipartite graphs, reversing time on one sublattice turns double bars into orientation-consistent reroutings, so the next-pin map is again a bijection and the spliced symbol applies unchanged; but the rest of the ferro proof (diffusive hole walk, spin-wave return energy) does not match AF physics (linear magnons).
candidates.adaptation_sketch: Orientation trick + spliced symbol for the pin test; new escape estimates needed.
candidates.expected_payoff: possible new Neel-order results for non-RP bipartite couplings

candidates.problem: Lorentz mirror model with loop weight 2 / spin-1/2 XXZ chain (discrete-time Brauer loops).
candidates.reference: K. Ryan, The spin-1/2 Heisenberg XXZ chain and the Lorentz mirror model with loop weight 2, arXiv:2608.21306 (Aug 2026).
candidates.status: recent; 1D results proved via six-vertex coupling; higher-d weight-2 mirror model open.
candidates.obstruction_match: Loop weight 2 is exactly what splicing produces; the mirror model is a Brauer-type loop model, so C1's Brauer symbol (stable, verified) applies in discrete time.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: Stable Brauer symbol per site (mirror = double bar / cross / pass mixture) and splicing; derive negative dependence of loop-hitting events.
candidates.expected_payoff: new correlation inequality for weight-2 mirror loops; not a resolution of the weight-1 mirror conjecture.

candidates.problem: NEGATIVE: loop models with weight theta != 2 (SU(n) / spin-1 bilinear-biquadratic, theta = 3; theta = 4 via two copies).
candidates.reference: Ueltschi 2013; Ueltschi et al., Neel order in the S=1 bilinear-biquadratic model via random loops, arXiv:1507.04942.
candidates.status: partly solved by RP for some parameters; device does not apply.
candidates.obstruction_match: Splicing yields weight tr(I_{C^2}) = 2. For theta = 4 one would need the doubled symbol E prod_i (x_i + y_{pi(i)})(x'_i + y'_{pi(i)}); numerically (this analysis, n = 3, random Bernoulli-transposition laws) it is NOT stable in 3/3 trials, while the single symbol is stable. Weighted contractions x_q = a t, y_q = b t give (a+b) per loop but path-dependent a,b factors.

candidates.problem: NEGATIVE: spatial random permutations / Feynman-Kac Bose gas (BEC as long cycles), permanental laws P(pi) ~ prod a_{i,pi(i)}.
candidates.reference: Betz & Ueltschi, spatial random permutations; Suto (long cycles).
candidates.obstruction_match: Would need stability of per[a_ij (x_i + y_j)]. Numerically (this analysis) it fails: near the 0/1 pattern {id, 3-cycle}, for one random positive 4x4 A, and for a Gaussian-kernel A (L = 0.5). Laws not generated by transpositions (uniform on 3-cycles) are also unstable. Also cycle weight there is 1, not 2.

candidates.problem: NEGATIVE/weak: unweighted interchange (theta = 1) infinite cycles in d = 3, 4 (Toth's 1993 conjecture; Elboim-Sly settle d >= 5).
candidates.obstruction_match: Splicing inevitably introduces weight 2 per avoided cycle; there is no stability-preserving contraction giving weight 1 (x_q = t, y_q = -t would give 0 but leaves the half-plane).
candidates.adaptation_sketch: none convincing; at most use theta=1 BBL stability for exclusion projections, which is old.
candidates.confidence: high (that it does not transfer directly)

candidates.problem: Permanent / immanant inequalities for laws on S_n (Carlen-Lieb-Loss type E_nu prod_i f_i(pi(i)) bounds; release family 238 four-row strict permanent inequality).
candidates.reference: Carlen, Lieb, Loss, An inequality of Hadamard type for permanents (2006); release family 238, A strict four-row permanent inequality and permutation moments.
candidates.obstruction_match: Superficial: the symbol is E_nu prod f_i(pi(i)) for the affine choice f_i(j) = x_i + y_j; stability of this restricted family gives subset negative dependence and Gurvits-capacity-type bounds only for transposition-generated laws, not the L^p permanent bounds needed there.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: Gurvits capacity lower bounds on P(pi(A) = B) for stable law symbols (coefficient of a real-stable polynomial >= k!/k^k times capacity).

in_family: Bloch's Law for Finite-Range Heisenberg Ferromagnets in Three Dimensions (Oct 5): sections/02-pins.tex L300-345 re-derives the layered symbol F_V, the splicing (x_q = y_q = t, linear coefficient, factor 2 at fixed points) and the output polynomial G_T, for finite-range anisotropic couplings (rates c_e = J_e/2).

The spherical magnetization law ... (Oct 5): sections/02-exchange.tex eq. stable-permutation-symbol and stable-presence (cites the September paper as [Ord], Lemmas 3.2-3.6); NEW USE: disk form E prod(1 + x_i y_{pi(i)}) with Asano-Ruelle contraction A + D for zero-free layered traces (Lemma trace-zero-free, L370-425), used for zero-free complex strips of the pressure.

The first lattice correction to Bloch's law (Oct 5): imports the pin estimates of the September paper (sections/02-loops.tex 'We state precisely the loop identities and pin estimates imported from ...'); no new use of the symbol itself.
other_families: Family 238 (Thorp shuffle): 'Routing densities and representation contraction for Thorp sweeps' sec 04-certificate and 'Compatibility entropy ...' introduction use the UNSPLICED ingredient (fair swaps preserve strongly Rayleigh occupancy; BBL Thms 4.9, 4.20) for negative association of occupancy bits. Same BBL inputs, not the spliced symbol; independent reuse of the precedent, not of the device.

No other family in CONTENTS.md uses permutation symbols, splicing, or cycle-weighted stability. Families 231 (strongly Rayleigh factors of IID) and 268 (spin-one Haldane gap) are thematically adjacent but do not use the device.
release_reuse.verdict: All reuse is within family 271 (same model, same lattice, same weight 2), plus one genuinely new in-family use (disk-form zero-freeness). No cross-family reuse of the spliced object.

earlier_equivalents: The law symbol E prod_i (x_i + y_{pi(i)}) is exactly the Borcea-Branden symbol G_T(z,w) = T[prod_i (z_i + w_i)] of the linear operator T f(y) = E f(y_{pi(.)}) on multiaffine polynomials (Borcea-Branden, Lee-Yang and Polya-Schur programs I, Invent. Math. 177 (2009), multiaffine symbol theorem). Its stability for Bernoulli-transposition and exclusion laws is equivalent to these operators preserving stability, which is BBL 2009 Thm 4.20/5.2. Nestoridi-Priestley-Schmid (arXiv:2304.02588, 2023) use precisely this symbol criterion for uniform block permutations.

The splicing step (identify the output variable of one layer with the input variable of the next and take the linear coefficient) is a composition of standard stability closure operations (diagonalization + differentiation + real specialization; BB II, Wagner's survey). Its use to take the TRACE of a layered product of two-site multiaffine transfer polynomials, giving a weight 2 per closed loop, is the half-plane counterpart of the Asano contraction used by Suzuki & Fisher (1971) for the quantum Heisenberg Lee-Yang theorem; the spherical companion itself calls its disk version 'a disk form of the contraction method of Asano and Ruelle'.

Not found: any prior use of the spliced symbol to obtain negative dependence (product bounds for simultaneous positive events) for the cycle-weighted theta=2 measure or for a next-pin permutation. Searches for stable polynomials + cycle-weighted interchange / Toth / Aizenman-Nachtergaele returned nothing combining them.
precedent_check.post_release_use: No use of the device outside the OAI release found after Oct 6, 2026 (searches: arXiv/web for 'spliced', 'stable permutation symbol', 'pin test', stable polynomial + Heisenberg/loop weight 2). The Aug 2026 paper of K. Ryan (arXiv:2608.21306) on loop weight 2 uses a six-vertex coupling, not stable polynomials.
precedent_check.verdict: The OBJECT is not new: it is the Borcea-Branden symbol of the permutation operator, and the contraction is a known Asano/Suzuki-Fisher-type trace. The new content is the BRIDGE: realizing that the trace contraction over unpinned layer points produces exactly the Toth weight 2 for cycles avoiding pins, so BBL negative dependence transfers from unweighted exchange to the pinned theta=2 measure. This supports downgrading E1 from 'N3 candidate' to N2 (new bridge with a constructed instantiation). The trace's 'against' note (writing prod(x_i + y_{pi(i)}) is close once stable polynomials are on the table) is confirmed and strengthened: the object is literally the standard BB symbol.

top5.title: Easy-plane XXZ ferromagnet / Ueltschi loop model, theta=2, u in (1/2,1)
top5.argument: This is the only open target where the obstruction matches exactly: theta = 2 loops, no reflection positivity (RP covers u <= 1/2; Betz-Klippel-Nauth 2025 still stop at u = 1/2), and long loops must be forced through a positivity-preserving bound on simultaneous avoidance events. I verified that the stability half extends: with crosses and double bars, the two-strand Brauer mixture symbol is Lorentzian, with eigenvalues 2, -2u, -2v, -2(1-u-v), so it is real stable for every admissible (u,v). Random Brauer laws stay stable numerically, and splicing still assigns 2 per closed loop. The extraction of a presence inequality for pairings (non-orientable loops) is genuinely missing, and the spin-wave/leakage half must be redone for an easy-plane model. If both close, this would be a real cross-model use of the device.

top5.title: Heisenberg ferromagnet magnetization on other transient graphs (trees of all degrees, nonamenable and polynomial-growth Cayley graphs, long-range couplings)
top5.argument: The device is graph-independent and transfers verbatim; the Bloch's-law companion already shows it absorbs anisotropic finite-range couplings without change. The open problems are real (ferromagnet, no RP; Bjornberg-Ueltschi handle trees only at large degree), and on trees and nonamenable graphs the geometric half (return fraction r small) should be easier than on Z^3. It ranks below C1 because it re-uses the device in the same model, so it is a weaker test of cross-problem power. It is also the most likely to succeed.

top5.title: Lee-Yang zero-freeness for quantum Heisenberg (Suzuki-Fisher re-proof; new zero-free strips)
top5.argument: The spherical companion already turns the symbol into a disk-form zero-freeness tool via Asano contraction. That is the only in-release use beyond the pin test, and it yields a measurable speedup target: SF71 takes about 12 pages with a Trotter classical mapping, against about 2 pages here. New zero-free regions (complex anisotropy, inhomogeneous fields) would feed Barvinok-type algorithms (HMS 2019). The weakness is that this direction is close to the Asano/Suzuki-Fisher precedent, so success says little about novelty.

top5.title: Negative dependence for exclusion and card shuffles (Liggett's inequality, BBL Thm 5.2 from deterministic starts, S_k shuffle SR)
top5.argument: These are the cleanest Lean-measurable held-out targets, and the OAI library already contains nearly everything: partial symmetrization, the law symbol, the Bernoulli step, limits and output extraction. Liggett's correlation inequality and the S_k-shuffle corollary become sub-page corollaries. The caveat is that the speedup comes from the UNSPLICED half, which is the Borcea-Branden symbol, so a positive speedup result would credit the precedent, not the eureka step. It is useful as a control.

top5.title: Poisson-Dirichlet PD(2) for Toth's theta=2 cycles on Z^d
top5.argument: This is the natural next open question in the same model. Negative dependence of loop-hitting under the weight-2 law is the missing structural input for split-merge comparison arguments, which Elboim-Sly replaced in the theta=1 case by a delicate random-walk coupling. Confidence is low: the pin test controls avoidance of pins, not the joint law of large cycles.

numerical_checks.script: scratchpad symbol_tests.py / symbol_tests2.py (not saved in repo); method: Branden's criterion (a real multiaffine polynomial is real stable iff all Rayleigh differences f_i f_j - f f_ij >= 0 on R^n), sampled at 3000-4000 random real points with mixed scales.
results: Two-strand Brauer mixture symbol (identity/cross/double bar with weights 1-u-v, u, v): stable at all six tested (u,v); proved for all admissible (u,v) via the Lorentzian eigenvalue computation {2, -2u, -2v, -2(1-u-v)}.
Random 3-strand Brauer laws (6 random steps, loop weight 2 at closed loops), 9 trials over three (u,v): all stable.
Doubled symbol (theta = 4 attempt) for random Bernoulli-transposition laws on 3 points: NOT stable in 3/3 trials (single symbol stable).

Permanental laws per[a_ij(x_i+y_j)]: stable for 5/5 random positive 3x3 A and 3/4 random positive 4x4 A; NOT stable near the 0/1 pattern {id, 3-cycle} (eps = 0.05), for one 4x4 A, and for a Gaussian-kernel A with L = 0.5.
Uniform law on the two 3-cycles, and identity-or-3-cycle: NOT stable; uniform S_3: stable.

Splicing identity checked symbolically: deleting a vertex of a 3-cycle gives (x0+y1)(x1+y0); deleting a fixed point gives 2(x0+y1)(x1+y0); weighted contraction x_q = a t, y_q = b t gives (a+b) per loop but a path-dependent factor (a x_i + b y_j), so the clean weight is a = b, i.e. theta = 2 only.

lean_source.name: Stable
lean_source.text:
def Stable {σ : Type*} (p : MvPolynomial σ ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ z ∈ Upper, MvPolynomial.eval z p ≠ 0
lean_source.note: Stability predicate used throughout (no zero on the open upper half-plane product). Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: permutationSymbol
lean_source.text:
def permutationSymbol (π : Equiv.Perm V) : MvPolynomial (V ⊕ V) ℂ :=
  ∏ i, (MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inl i) + MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inr (π i)))
lean_source.note: THE ITEM: F_pi(x,y) = prod_i (x_i + y_{pi(i)}) over variables V ⊕ V. No docstring in source. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: stable_permutationSymbol
lean_source.text: lemma stable_permutationSymbol (π : Equiv.Perm V) : Stable (permutationSymbol π) := by
lean_source.note: Deterministic symbol is stable. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: lawSymbol
lean_source.text:
def lawSymbol (μ : Ω → ℝ) (π : Ω → Equiv.Perm V) : MvPolynomial (V ⊕ V) ℂ :=
  ∑ ω, MvPolynomial.C (μ ω : ℂ) * permutationSymbol (π ω)
lean_source.note: Expected symbol E F_pi for a finite law mu on permutations. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: stable_lawSymbol_bernoulli
lean_source.text:
theorem stable_lawSymbol_bernoulli (μ : Ω → ℝ) (π : Ω → Equiv.Perm V)
    (hs : Stable (lawSymbol μ π)) (i j : V) {u : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ u) (h1 : u ≤ 1) :
    Stable (lawSymbol (fun z : Bool × Ω => (if z.1 then u else 1 - u) * μ z.2)
      (fun z : Bool × Ω => (if z.1 then Equiv.swap i j else 1) * π z.2)) := by
lean_source.note: Composing with an independent Bernoulli(u) transposition preserves stability (partial symmetrization). Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: stable_lawSymbol_limit
lean_source.text:
theorem stable_lawSymbol_limit {ι : Type*} {φ : Filter ι} [φ.NeBot]
    (μ : ι → Ω → ℝ) (ν : Ω → ℝ) (π : Ω → Equiv.Perm V)
    (hc : ∀ ω, Filter.Tendsto (fun i => μ i ω) φ (nhds (ν ω)))
    (hν : ∑ ω, ν ω = 1) (hs : ∀ᶠ i in φ, Stable (lawSymbol (μ i) π)) :
    Stable (lawSymbol ν π) := by
lean_source.note: Limits of stable law symbols are stable (Hurwitz). Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: stable_outputSymbol
lean_source.text:
theorem stable_outputSymbol (μ : Ω → ℝ) (π : Ω → Equiv.Perm V)
    (hμ : ∑ ω, μ ω ≠ 0) (hs : Stable (lawSymbol μ π)) (T : Finset V) :
    Stable (outputSymbol μ (fun ω => π ω) T) := by
lean_source.note: Output extraction: the subset generating polynomial of pi(T) is stable. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: spliceVariables
lean_source.text:
def spliceVariables : Option V ⊕ Option V → Option (V ⊕ V)
  | Sum.inl none => none
  | Sum.inr none => none
  | Sum.inl (some i) => some (Sum.inl i)
  | Sum.inr (some i) => some (Sum.inr i)
lean_source.note: Identifies the input and output variable of the deleted vertex (none) into one variable t. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: eraseNone
lean_source.text:
def eraseNone {σ : Type*} : MvPolynomial (Option σ) ℂ →ₐ[ℂ] MvPolynomial σ ℂ :=
  MvPolynomial.aeval (fun j => j.elim 0 MvPolynomial.X)
lean_source.note: Sets t = 0 after differentiation. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: splice
lean_source.text:
def splice (p : MvPolynomial (Option V ⊕ Option V) ℂ) : MvPolynomial (V ⊕ V) ℂ :=
  eraseNone (MvPolynomial.pderiv none (MvPolynomial.rename spliceVariables p))
lean_source.note: THE SPLICING OPERATION: identify x_q = y_q = t, take the linear coefficient in t. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: spliceWeight
lean_source.text: def spliceWeight (π : Equiv.Perm (Option V)) : ℝ := if π none = none then 2 else 1
lean_source.note: Weight 2 when the deleted vertex is a fixed point (closed cycle), else 1. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: splice_permutationSymbol
lean_source.text:
lemma splice_permutationSymbol (π : Equiv.Perm (Option V)) :
    splice (permutationSymbol π) =
      MvPolynomial.C (spliceWeight π : ℂ) * permutationSymbol (Equiv.removeNone π) := by
lean_source.note: Defining property: splicing a deterministic symbol gives spliceWeight times the symbol of the spliced permutation. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: stable_spliced_law
lean_source.text:
theorem stable_spliced_law (μ : Ω → ℝ) (π : Ω → Equiv.Perm (Option V))
    (hμ : ∀ ω, 0 ≤ μ ω) (hpos : 0 < ∑ ω, μ ω) (hs : Stable (lawSymbol μ π)) :
    Stable (lawSymbol (fun ω => μ ω * spliceWeight (π ω))
      (fun ω => Equiv.removeNone (π ω))) := by
lean_source.note: Splicing preserves stability of a law symbol, producing the weight-2 reweighted law. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: cycle_weight_splice
lean_source.text:
theorem cycle_weight_splice (π : Perm (Option V)) (P : Set V) :
    (2 : ℝ) ^ missingCount π (some '' P) =
      (if π none = none then 2 else 1) * (2 : ℝ) ^ missingCount (removeNone π) P := by
lean_source.note: Combinatorial identity: deleting one unpinned vertex multiplies 2^{#cycles missing pins} correctly. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: pinLaw
lean_source.note: Spliced symbol F_P = E[2^{n_P} prod_{i in P}(x_i + y_{sigma(i)})] of the next-pin permutation. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: stable_pinLaw
lean_source.text:
theorem stable_pinLaw {V : Type u} [Fintype V] (μ : Ω → ℝ) (π : Ω → Perm V)
    (hμ : ∀ ω, 0 ≤ μ ω) (hpos : 0 < ∑ ω, μ ω) (hs : Stable (lawSymbol μ π))
    (P : Set V) : Stable (pinLaw μ π P) := by
lean_source.note: Key lemma: the spliced pin-law symbol is stable for every pin set P. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: stable_symmetrize
lean_source.text:
theorem stable_symmetrize {p : MvPolynomial σ ℂ} (hp : Stable p)
    (hm : MultiAffine p) (i j : σ) {u : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ u) (h1 : u ≤ 1) :
    Stable (symmetrize p i j u) := by
lean_source.note: Partial symmetrization closure lemma (BBL Thm 4.20 analogue). Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: presence_product
lean_source.text:
theorem presence_product {μ : Finset σ → ℝ} (hμ : ∀ A, 0 ≤ μ A)
    (h₁ : presence μ ∅ = 1) (hs : Stable (presencePolynomial μ ∅))
    (J : Finset σ) : presence μ J ≤ ∏ j ∈ J, presence μ {j} := by
lean_source.note: Presence inequality from stability (BBL Thm 4.9 consequence). Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.

lean_source.name: finite_simultaneous_pin_test
lean_source.text:
theorem finite_simultaneous_pin_test (μ : Ω → ℝ) (π : Ω → Equiv.Perm V)
    (hμ : ∀ ω, 0 ≤ μ ω) (hpos : 0 < ∑ ω, μ ω) (hs : Stable (lawSymbol μ π))
    (E : Set V) (T : Finset V) (hT : T.Nonempty) (hET : Disjoint E (T : Set V)) :
    (∑ ω, if ∀ i ∈ T, ¬ HasHit (π ω) E i then pinDensity μ π E ω else 0) ≤
      (2 * returnFraction μ π E T) ^ T.card := by
lean_source.note: Decisive use: P_E(T on cycles avoiding E) <= (2 r)^{|T|}. Text is verbatim source lines; proofs (after `:= by`) omitted.
